description: Fixed evaluation surface for the Pokemon code-policy family. Train decks and train opponents are visible in the workspace and are the agent's feedback signal. The heldout split is sealed: only its shape is published here.

train.pairing: ordered deck pairs: the candidate pilots candidate_deck, the opponent pilots opponent_deck; side is the seat

heldout.deck_pool: Authored from the RS/SS card pool. The five train decks draw only on CG/DF, so no heldout deck shares a non-Energy card with any agent-visible deck.
heldout.provenance_note: Heldout opponents lift JoshuaPurtell/engine-bench-tcg algo_bench results, which are public. Sealing covers the composition of the split - which policies, which decks, which cells, which seeds - not the secrecy of any individual source file. Receipts must not claim source-level secrecy. 8 of 11 upstream policies are used; 3 were dropped because they need behaviour-changing rewrites to compile against the current engine ABI rather than the mechanical port the builder applies.
heldout.pairing: ordered deck pairs: the candidate pilots candidate_deck, the opponent pilots opponent_deck; side is the seat

baseline_policy_note: The baseline is the RANKING ORIGIN: reward is candidate - baseline over identical cells, so an incompetent baseline makes every candidate look good and the benchmark measures nothing. reference_policy_v2 measures 64.9% cell win rate over this train surface and beats every train opponent; the previous origin, candidates/reference/baseline_policy.rs (TemplateAi), measured 28.9% and lost to all five. See docs/pokemon_code_policy_reference.md for the per-opponent table.
